data.name: Maanasa
data.gender_notes: Maanasa is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘manas’ (mind) and ‘asana’ (seat), Maanasa signifies the seat of thoughts, emotions, and sensations. In Hindu mythology, it is the name of a river in the Himalayas, believed to be the abode of Lord Shiva. The name Maanasa carries the meaning “Mind, Thought, Sensation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maanasa usually hope their child will grow to embody mind, thought, sensation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes deep introspection and inner peace.
data.etymology: Maanasa belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mind, Thought, Sensation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maanasa total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Maanasa stands as an important name in Hindu mythology and culture, representing the power of thoughts and emotions. It is an auspicious name, revered for its spiritual meaning as the 'seat of the mind.' In Hindu rituals and practices, the mind is considered the most powerful tool to connect with the divine. Hence, the name Maanasa carries a deep significance in Hinduism, highlighting the importance of mindfulness and inner reflection.
data.spiritual_significance: Maanasa holds immense spiritual importance in Hinduism, symbolizing the connection between the human mind and the divine consciousness. This name is believed to be a reflection of Lord Shiva's cosmic consciousness as the universal mind. By invoking the name Maanasa, one seeks to connect with the divine mind and achieve inner peace and enlightenment. In Hindu philosophy, the ultimate goal is to merge one's individual consciousness with the universal consciousness - Maanasa.
